main_message: Small 2-4 unit apartment buildings nearly vanished from new construction, and three sets of rules (zoning maps, single-staircase fire codes, and bank lending categories) plus costs and interest rates all play a part. Changing just one rule, like zoning, hasn't brought them back yet, and nobody can say how much each factor matters.
why_hook: The 1-in-13 versus 1-in-100 contrast is striking and the 'why' question is clear. But it's followed right away by a disclaimer, and it's a dry topic.
mechanisms_in_your_words: 1) Zoning maps: most residential land only allows single-family houses, and parking rules eat up small lots. 2) Stairwell/fire code: taller walk-ups need two staircases, which takes space and money. 3) Bank lending: loans for 1-4 units work like house loans, but 5 or more units, or a shop in the building, make financing hard. 4) Costs, interest rates and rents might make the numbers not work anyway. The three rules are presented as parallel 'locks' with a fourth economic factor on top, rather than as a chain where each causes the next.
ending_comment: It gives a layered answer (the three rules plus costs) and admits the record can't say how much each matters. That's honest, but I was left without a clear 'because of X'.

confusing.why: Unclear how this chapter links back to the three locks.
Unclear whether it applies to 2-4 unit buildings. It says 3+ units, so triplexes are affected, which seems to contradict 'a plain duplex or triplex usually isn't affected'.

Fine as data, but the video gives no cause for the drop, so I may infer one it doesn't support.

claims_you_doubt.why: Not a doubt about accuracy, but I don't see why it matters to the argument.

questions_left_unanswered: How much of the decline is due to rules versus costs and interest rates?
Why did the steepest fall happen in the late 1980s?
Did anything in the 1980s change, such as savings and loan failures, tax rules or lending?
Why do big buildings of 50+ units now dominate?
What would a person actually have to do to build one today?
Do these buildings cost less to rent than other housing?
Why is the lending line at four, and why hasn't it changed?
best_moment: [00] The one-in-thirteen versus one-in-a-hundred contrast; it hooked me. [07] is also good for admitting 'the record we found doesn't measure that split'.
top3_fixes: Cut the 1920s court-case detail (seg 02) and the code editions and percentages in seg 04 down to one example each, and add a simple visual or table of 'which rule hits which building'.
Explain the 1986-1990 collapse in seg 08, or say outright that no cause is known. It's the biggest drop in the video and it's just left hanging.
Make the opening question more personal, e.g. 'Why can't you find a duplex or fourplex to rent or buy in new construction?', and fix the confusing triplex/commercial-code inconsistency in seg 04.
